I just overcame a 4-month existential crisis [SEP] This post is for you if you are currently dealing with existential dread. I really wish I would have read this somewhere when I was suffering through it recently. I am 31 years old in my life has recently changed completely. I went from owning a debt collection agency in New York to being a software engineer in California, I left a six year long relationship, I sold my house and business, I sold my car, and I got back in shape after letting myself go. All of this sounds very positive but it was a huge shock to my system. I feel like I had a midlife crisis at 30 because the reality that time keeps moving forward bringing me closer to death finally set in. I realized that I wasted my 20s in a bad relationship, and I am roughly 10 years clean from a bad heroin addiction. I couldn't help but feel like I've wasted my entire adult life even if I'm on the right track now, I should be further ahead in life. Of course you can argue that I'm doing well for myself but the feeling of not living up to my own expectations, and the fear of never finding a wife or starting a family was terrifying, it is still terrifying. I got to a point where the only thing I was ever thinking about was my own mortality, the actual fact that I was actually going to die someday, and confronting my lack of spirituality. My mother is a very religious person and my father died when I was a teenager. I never got to talk to my father about these things, and my mother is so confident in an eternal afterlife that I envy her but I can't believe the same thing. I had talked about this with a therapist that I really trust and respect. The best that he could tell me is that the universe existed for billions of years without me and everything was just fine, and that everyone is going to die so it's the most natural thing in the world. None of that made me feel any better because as insignificant as my life might be to the universe, my life is the most significant thing ever to me. So relatively speaking, there's no solace there. I've never had suicidal ideations and I'm not going to say that this existential crisis caused me to feel that, because that would be counterintuitive. But I think I can finally understand the mindset that a suicidal person might experience because my very existence was torturous for about 4 months. I would talk to everyone I knew to try to figure out how other people cope with this but I realize that the majority of people just don't fixate on this. I think that your own mortality is just a vague concept that people think that they've accepted but in reality, very few people need to wrestle with that reality when they are young. The good news that I wanted to share with everyone is that it's gone. The existential dread, the never-ending impending sense of Doom and terror that I lived with for 4 months straight finally let go of me. I'm still distressed by the same thoughts but I'm not so fixated on it that I can't function or find happiness. I moved to a city where psilocybin mushrooms were decriminalized and even sold over the counter in dispensaries. I hadn't tripped on mushrooms since I was 18 but I had a gut feeling that it's what I needed to fix this. Don't get discouraged if that's not something that you are up for because I do genuinely believe now that the obsession would have passed with time, it may have taken a little bit more time but I've been skateboarding and I think that has been extremely healthy for me both physically and mentally. I would encourage anyone who is struggling with existential dread to pick up something you're passionate about as a kid because when you are a kid you pursue things for pure happiness instead of money. For what it's worth, one relatively low dose mushroom trip was enough to turn the volume on those intrusive thoughts down significantly. It gave me a sense of spirituality and a sense of being part of something greater than myself. I think I'm going to make a point to do it roughly once every year as a form of maintenance. Just now that if you are struggling with existential dread, it feels like there is no end in sight but having just escaped from it, I want to share a little bit of Hope with everyone. Hang in there. It will be okay.

My therapist cried in a session and another therapist told me to quit her ASAP [SEP] I have been seeing my therapist for a few years but just started recently feeling comfortable enough to open up about my past trauma to her. Upon doing so, she cried. She did try to hold it back but eventually she cried then immediately apologized and told me that I remind her of her daughter and she cares about me. It honestly was the first time I've felt love from a parental figure. However, during that time I was actually having a mental breakdown. I was reliving my trauma everyday and it impacted my work greatly. My boss was not understanding and my physichiatrist eventually recommended a extensive therapy group with a "great therapist." This therapist was not at all what I expected. She was incredibly into the "tough love" approach. She made everyone go in a circle and talk about their most traumatic moments. I have social anxiety and these were strangers so I did not really participate in that. But I did talk about my therapy experience and my coping mechanisms and such. She eventually found out that my therapist cried once in a session. She told me that was "beyond unprofessional" and that I should "drop her immediately." I actually did end up dropping her only to get a horrible experience with another therapist. One recommended by the therapist that told me to drop my initial therapist. I was so sad and eventually went back to my initial therapist. I haven't seen anything wrong but I can't get help but feel insecure about my own decision. Am I making the right choice? Is it okay to go to someone cause they feel like a friend you can open up to? Are emotions bad and unprofessional for a therapist to express? *LIL' UPDATE* Wow! Thank you all so much for the comments and awards. It was so nice to read all of your experiences, I'm so overwhelmed with happiness rn to not feel so alone! I have seen 8 therapists in my life and I have never felt this comfortable with one. It honestly was the first time I haven't regretted telling a professional my personal trauma. Although not everyone agrees with this approach, her emotion ultimately showed me that I have people that care about me and it really helped me in a time when I really just needed compassion. With that being said, I am continuing to see my empathetic therapist as that is what works best for me. Thank you again for all of your reassurance and encouragement in helping me choose what's best for me. I struggle a lot with decision making so I was really in my head about this. Anywho, just wanted to say you are part of a wonderful community here and I hope you all find happiness/peace. I'm not there quite yet, but baby steps are okay.

Struggling with death anxiety and meaninglessness [SEP] (This is a very long stream of consciousness rant with no cohesion whatsoever) I_x0019_m 21 and in college and in the last few months have begun suffering from constant, pervasive death anxiety that has led to me becoming depressed, and seriously reckoning with mental health really for the first time in my life. I_x0019_m seeing therapy and trying out medications but so far have not found any meaningful relief. I don_x0019_t say this to brag, but I am, and have always been a very philosophical, cerebral, intellectual-oriented person, and that_x0019_s what has driven me to my current situation. I read a lot about religious studies and mythology, because that stuff is extremely interesting to me, but a huge component of religious belief is beliefs about death, afterlife, soul, reasons for humanity_x0019_s existence, etc. I_x0019_ve been an atheist since middle school and previously found myself very comfortable with my views, but for some reason reading so much about the topic of religion - specifically with the thought that *every one of them is wrong* in mind - gave me what I would call an existential crisis, because it really impressed upon me in a way I_x0019_ve never felt before that *holy shit, death is the end and we really aren_x0019_t here for any reason at all*. And to me that_x0019_s horrifying. The problem isn_x0019_t that death feels like an escape, as I see is posted a lot on this subreddit, but the exact opposite: I *like* being alive, that_x0019_s why I_x0019_m *terrified* of dying. I like the college I_x0019_m at, and am interested in the things I am learning. I have great friends who I like spending time with and can count on to be there for me. There are passions and pastimes I get enjoyment out of and want to keep doing. This just makes me feel like *I have so much to lose by dying*. I had previously felt, quite securely, that many old adages about death were true: that there_x0019_s no reason to fear death because I was dead for 13.8 billion years and wasn_x0019_t bothered by it and since won_x0019_t be bothered by it after I_x0019_m dead either, that I_x0019_ll never really live if I_x0019_m afraid of dying, etc. Carpe diem. Memento Mori. In essence: that death is nothing to me because death is itself an imperceptible state of unconsciousness. But now, that feels like a threat, a permanent and total annihilation of my self, which nullifies all meaning in life. If death is inevitable, and it is the end, then what_x0019_s the point of anything? It_x0019_s one thing to believe that I can make a mark on the world, that I can contribute in some way to the progress of humanity, but in academia they say, progress is a myth, and humanity itself is doomed anyway no matter what. Nothing lasts, everyone who lives will die, humanity is a random cosmic fluke, the Sun will eventually blow up the earth if we don_x0019_t drive ourselves extinct first, the final end state of the universe is probably eternal nothingness in which literally nothing can ever happen again. The very notion that one_x0019_s brain can randomly suffer from a genetic chemical imbalance that alters their ability to think and feel is itself so absurd. The thought that the universe is indifferent to us is so crushing, like a cruel truth we were never meant to know, the most sick joke ever played. Even if I do have a soul and there is something like a heaven, I don_x0019_t want to be a disembodied soul! I don_x0019_t want to spend eternity in endless bliss in union with God or something! I want to be *here*, in this fascinating world, with these people I love, without having to worry about our bodies crumbling away or our planet dying. Immortality isn_x0019_t an option we have, and even if we had that, unless we outline many precise conditions for it, it would also become unbearable. So there is no good option. Eternal life is bad and death is bad. The universe set us up to lose. I know it_x0019_s pointless, but I can_x0019_t help but wonder about it: Why did I have to be born in the period of human history where we knew these harsh realities, when instead I could have been born somewhen, somewhere else with greater religiosity, and I would be able to indulge the wishful thinking of afterlives, divine cosmic purpose, a meaning for suffering? No, I have to live in _x001C_modernity_x001D_, when not only is capitalism making people miserable and killing the planet and I can_x0019_t do anything about it, but I have to reconcile with modern science_x0019_s bitter truths. I never asked to be born, let alone in this time and place, and so surely I never asked to deal with this wretched fucking human condition. I know, on an intuitive level, that I don_x0019_t have to feel this way, that I can be happy even though I know I_x0019_m gonna die, which most other people, including other atheists, seem to be capable of. But even when I think of living the ideal of a long, happy, and successful life, in which I achieved my life goals, have no regrets, cultivated a lasting legacy, can die happy, even then, I will still have to age, and wither, and *die*, and there_x0019_s nothing I can do about it. We are all so utterly powerless. And that assumes I even get that far; people say _x001C_you are so young! You have so much time!_x001D_ And all I can feel is *you don_x0019_t know that*. Random chance, no matter how unlikely, can cut my life short at any time. I_x0019_m not even guaranteed 80 years of life! I could get cancer in my 50s or get hit by a car in a week. Even so, the notion that I_x0019_m young and therefore shouldn_x0019_t be worrying about death - indeed, wasting my finite time - isn_x0019_t particularly helpful either; punting the problem down the road to suffer over it later doesn_x0019_t exactly resolve it! I had previously found myself believing in something akin to existentialism, that is, that none of us are born for any intrinsic purpose or divine plan and that we must find and make our own meaning in life. That felt freeing, self-determining. I make my own fate, I_x0019_m in charge of my destiny, it isn_x0019_t God just telling us what to do. But now I just feel like, isn_x0019_t that subjective meaning illusory, a product of our stupid animal brains connecting dots where there aren_x0019_t any to trick itself into feeling better? I have even been trying to look back into spirituality and faith to feel better, going back over modern arguments for God or the soul, but there_x0019_s always the voice in the back of my head that says, you know this is irrational, you know you cannot fool yourself into believing any of this, no matter how much you want to. In school, I read all about theories in disciplines that claim that pretty much everything is arbitrary: one of the fundamental ideas of linguistics is that all language, all communication at all, is arbitrary; anthropological theory says, cultures are merely social constructions invented to serve biological functions; psychology says, evolutionary biology explains largely how our brains work, including our need for meaning, our drive to interpret signs and symbols that don_x0019_t exist, to find connection and patterns that aren_x0019_t there. Of course, postmodern theory even posits that there is no such thing as fixed, non-arbitrarily filtered or expressed truth at all! If you strip all of these things down, what am I left with that_x0019_s real? *Nothing*. How do I even know *anything* is real? Nothing means anything. That_x0019_s all there is, evolution wants us to keep making babies over and over, we_x0019_re not here for any other reason and that_x0019_s all our bodies are designed to do. Science reduces everything down and removes all meaning, and we found that there is nothing special about our place in the universe, that our minds are not perfect souls but brains that can be deeply flawed or compromised because of its genetic makeup or physical experiences. God and gods are just overactive theories of mind attributing causation we don_x0019_t understand to agents we can_x0019_t see, the scientists think, God is just a psychological self-projection of ourselves and our own values, another theory goes. Religious experiences, mysticism, NDEs? Just certain activations of the brain by certain chemicals. _x001C_Mind opening_x001D_ _x001C_spiritual_x001D_ drugs just do similar things to the brain and thus produce similar effects. Then there_x0019_s stuff like Terror Management Theory and the works of philosophical pessimism by writers like Thomas Ligotti or Peter Wessel Zapffe, who postulate that all of the subjective meaning we make, all culture (including religion), can be summed up as a system of symbols invented to distract and delude us from the existential horror of death, that our advanced consciousness is a curse because it is deeply hard-wired to reject or deny these horrible truths, which is maybe the most depressing idea I_x0019_ve ever read (and it doesn_x0019_t appear to be wrong to me). David Benatar sums it up: better never to have been at all. People say, _x001C_well even so, if death is the end, you can be happy *now*_x001D_ and in my head I just think why even *be* happy, why even *value* it? It_x0019_s just some behavioral mechanism evolution programmed our brains with to help us survive long enough to procreate. It_x0019_s literally just a chemical! _x001C_God is Love!_x001D_ Love is just a different set of chemicals. There isn_x0019_t anything more to it than that. I_x0019_m a bunch of neurons firing in a slowly but surely decaying prison of flesh programmed by billions of years of mutation and death. I may be in control of my choices (or, fuck, who knows, some people think science proves hard determinism is true, wouldn_x0019_t that be worse&) but I can_x0019_t choose a different state of existence, I can_x0019_t be anything other than human, and to be human is to be mortal. Something I keep going back to is the idea that this is all so inherently ridiculous that it *must* have been designed this way, like these circumstances are actually TOO cruel or TOO meaningless to not have been intentionally designed by God, or the aliens running the simulation, or whatever. Like, there_x0019_s no way we built all of this just to spin out and be reduced to nothing, right? Surely there_x0019_s no way the circumstances of the universe aligned so randomly to allow us to exist, to allow ME to exist, only to find out that we are nothing, at the precise time and place for all of these ideas to be exposed to and coalesce in me. Maybe this is all just for *me*, intricately designed for *my journey* - but even the small amount of solace I could take in the seduction of solipsism is followed by the horror that everyone else I care about would then turn out to be unreal, so that_x0019_s not a way out either. That_x0019_s just horrible in a slightly different way. And I know, on some level, that I don_x0019_t really believe this, otherwise, why would I enjoy my life enough to not want it to end? There are still things I want to do, feel, accomplish: I want to write and find success as an author, learn so much more about the topics I_x0019_m interested in, consume more art and play more video games, spend more time with my loved ones, see more of the world, experience the love of finding a romantic life partner, fuck, I_x0019_m a virgin and I want to know what sex feels like! But I fear that all of these desires are insignificant to the universe, stupid programmed evolutionary instincts, arbitrary illusions I only value because of the culture I was raised in and therefore meaningless, and most of all, that I won_x0019_t have enough time to do them, enough time, in the most literal sense, being my Self. And therein lies the paradox of it all, I do think life is worth living, but my fear of death and nihilism are destroying my will to live, and I don_x0019_t know how to claw my way out of this contradiction yet. I feel so hopeless and powerless. I just needed to get all of this off my chest in a space outside of therapy. I don_x0019_t know what kind of responses I_x0019_m hoping to get from people by posting here.

Loki's Wager for Determinism [SEP] Much of the debate around determinism focuses on a question we, as finite beings, can never definitively answer: Is the universe *truly* deterministic? I'd like to propose a more pragmatic approach. Instead of asking what is ultimately true, let's ask: **What is the most productive belief for a mind committed to inquiry?** When we encounter a surprise... an event we can't explain, from a human choice to commit murder to the initial asymmetry of the universe or the outcome of the spin measurement of an electron... we face a fork in the road. # The Two Paths: Epistemic vs. Ontological Surprise 1. **Ontological Surprise:** We can conclude the event was fundamentally and irreducibly random. This is the path of indeterminism. As an explanation, it is a "just so" statement that results in a dead end. The inquiry stops. 2. **Epistemic Surprise:** We can conclude our model of reality is incomplete. This is the path of methodological determinism. It's the disciplined attitude of saying, "oh, I must not have the full story yet". This assumption fuels the endless search for a deeper explanation. Since we are finite beings, and our ignorance of all the facts is always a possible explanation for our inability to accurately predict, we can never know for sure which path reflects reality. We can analyze the choice as a wager like the one Pascal constructed. The goal isn't salvation, in the orthodox sense, but the continued pursuit of knowledge. # The Wager for Inquiry: Let's lay out the grid of possibilities. The consequences below aren't about being "right" or "wrong" in an absolute sense, but about the impact on the process of discovery itself. There are four classes kind of like the exhaustive outcomes of flipping two coins. The two coins are 1) your belief in determinism (e.g. *belief* that it is true or false) and 2) the nature of reality (e.g. determinism is *actually* true or false). The table of options and its consequences looks like the following: |...|Reality is Truly Deterministic|Reality is Truly Indeterministic| |:-|:-|:-| |**You Believe in Determinism**|**Productive Outcome**: You are on the correct path. You "keep digging until you get to the complete story". Science proceeds until the asymptotic predictability of everything.|**Productive Outcome**: You're on a perpetual search. You never stop looking and build statistical mechanics models that are useful... and build cool stuff. No harm no foul.| |**You Believe in Indeterminism**|**Worst Outcome L**: You incorrectly stop seeking an answer, falsely believing you have the final, uncaused answer. Science is terminated.|**Correct Dead End Outcome**: You happen to be correct. You've accepted "it's random" as the final explanation and can never justify this step in the face of our finitude.| # The Asymmetrical Consequences As the wager shows, the risks are completely **asymmetrical**. * **Believing in determinism** is the low-risk, high-reward bet. The worst-case scenario is a perpetual but productive search for knowledge. It never halts inquiry. Note: This does not preclude the usefulness of statistical models for predicting outcomes of experiments or modeling processes. * **Believing in indeterminism** is the high-risk, low-reward bet. In both outcomes, the search for a deeper explanation ends. You either stop incorrectly (the worst error) or stop with an unsatisfying, unjustifiable "truth" but never truly being able to know if you are correct or not. If you value the continuous search for new effective knowledge (e.g. if you value Science), the most rational and effective approach is to make the leap of faith into determinism. It's the only belief that obligates us to keep searching. The wager isn't just a bet on determinism; it's a bet on the existence of a deeper story and the value of inquiry. And while this methodological approach is technically agnostic on the actual determinism of the cosmos, the belief in our finitude is fundamental and unchanging. We will never be un-finite minds and we will never be able to construct an infinite mind. This means that equivocating on the actual nature of reality is irrelevant and it is thus safe and most pragmatic to simply make the leap of faith into determinism belief. As Loki put it in the opening of the Avenger's movie: >I come with glad tidings, of a world made free. >"Free from what," you ask? >Freedom. Freedom is life's great lie. Once you accept that, in your heart... You will know peace.

The kind of determinism relevant to this discussion [SEP] Let_x0019_s start with a general definition of determinism: _x001C_a specified physical state of the world at time *t* entails all states at times < *t* and > *t* by causation_x001D_. I propose this definition not as my own, but to highlight some aspects of it that are not relevant to this discussion. One by one, I will pare off parts of this definition that I believe are orthogonal and irrelevant to this discussion, so that we may isolate the minimum viable kind of determinism that libertarianism must deny. **_x001D_specified_x001D_**: The word "specified" smuggles an epistemic concept (what can be known, calculated, or described by an observer) into what should be a strictly ontological claim (how reality actually operates). The threat to libertarianism does not depend on whether Laplace_x0019_s Demon or a supercomputer can actually specify or predict the state of the universe. It only matters that the state (and corresponding behaviour) is definitively fixed and necessitated. **_x001D_physical_x001D_**: Philosophy of mind seems to be a red herring to the discussion of determinism. It is tempting to think that if we disavow materialism and adopt dualism, we have successfully rescued libertarianism. This is a misconception in my view _x0014_ I call it the [Soul of the Gaps]( Even if the human mind is composed of a non-physical substance or an immaterial soul, it does not follow that the substance is necessarily indeterministic and not governed by deterministic laws. The notion that threatens libertarianism is necessitation of behaviour/states, not whether they are physically or mentally instantiated. **_x001C_< t_x001D_**: The simplest way I can put this is by analogy: The state of the grid in Conway_x0019_s Game of Life at time *t* along with Conway_x0019_s laws strictly entails all future states. Yet, the system is irreversible; multiple distinct initial configurations can evolve to the same configuration. Because of this many-to-one mapping, historical information is irretrievably lost as time moves forward. If you are handed a specific grid state at time *t*, it is often impossible to retrodict the past state. Now, imagine that you are a cell in Conway_x0019_s Game of Life. Is it possible for you to have libertarian free will purely by virtue of the fact that the past state of the world cannot be retrodicted? I would assume the answer is a resounding no. A many-to-one mapping that evolves in a fixed manner seems to pose the same threat to libertarianism as a one-to-one mapping. **_x001D_by causation_x001D_**: Causation carries centuries of philosophical baggage. By including this in the definition, we seem to risk bogging down our analysis into secondary disputes such as Humean constant conjunction or Aristotelian final causes. Again, what seems to be the threat to libertarianism is the fixity of future states and behaviour, not the mechanism of such necessitation. **A pared-down definition:** We have arrived at a pared-down version of determinism that seems to most clearly isolate the threat to libertarianism: _x001C_The state of the world at time *t* entails all states at times > *t*._x001D_

is the "problem of interaction" a real problem? [SEP] One of the arguments I most often read against dualism is the "problem of interaction." How can a (hypothetical) incorporeal, non-objectified, transcendent willor whateverinfluence and interact causally with organs, objects, limbs, the brain, etc.? However, the same proponents of this alleged incompatibility usually believe that there are laws in nature that influence, determine, direct, impose, and causally constrain various objects, atoms, molecules, and bodies of physical matter. Similarly, they believe that there are logical principles that require things to be and behave in a certain way (for example, the principle of non-contradiction). Likewise, mathematical principles and truths. Now, physical laws and logical-mathematical principles, strictly speaking, do not seem to me to be physical objects. They are not in the least interactable and directly observable. They do not have specific positions in space, time, mass, or energy values. I don't say that they are not physical, but surely they exist on a completely different level than tables or rainstorms. Their presence and their effects are... inferable from the behavior of stuff we empirically observe and perceive, but they themselves are not manipulable and perceivable in the same ways. But that doesn't mean they are beyond any interaction: math and logic can be apprehended, known, manipulated; we can be quite creative using them. The same with the laws of physics; the fundamental ones are not modifiable, but we can manipulate them, combine them in various ways to give rise to marvelous stuff and original (emergent) behaviors. So free will is kinda "the law that a conscious organism gives to himself," and a choice kinda like the outcome of an equation, the result of a process happening in the realm of reason... yeah, sure, you cannot observe those things under the microscope, see them, touch them, hit them with charged particles in the LHC. That doesn't mean they don't exist or they don't/can't interact and have causal efficacy.

Finding Free Will in a Deterministic Universe [SEP] After my father died, I spent time in the public library, browsing the philosophy section. I think I was reading something by Baruch Spinoza that introduced the issue of determinism as a threat to free will. I found this troublesome until I had this thought experiment (whether I read it in one of the books or just came up with it myself, I can_x0019_t recall). The idea that my choices were inevitable bothered me, so I considered how I might escape what seemed like an external control. It struck me that all I needed to do was to wait till I had a decision to make, between A and B, and if I felt myself leaning heavily toward A, I would simply choose B instead. So easy! But then it occurred to me that my desire to thwart inevitability had caused B to become the inevitable choice, so I would have to switch back to A again, but then & it was an infinite loop! No matter which I chose, inevitability would continue to switch to match my choice! Hmm. So, who was controlling the choice, me or inevitability? Well, the concern that was driving my thought process was my own. Inevitability was not some entity driving this process for its own reasons. And I imagined that if inevitability were such an entity, it would be sitting there in the library laughing at me, because it made me go through these gyrations without doing anything at all, except for me thinking about it. My choice may be a deterministic event, but it was an event where I was actually the one doing the choosing. And that is what free will is really about: is it me or is someone or something else making the decision. It was always really me. And since the solution was so simple, I no longer gave it any thought. Then much later, a few years ago, I ran into some on-line discussions about it, and I wondered why it was still a problem for everyone else, since I had seen through the paradox more than fifty years ago.

Virtue as dancing rather than archery [SEP] Virtue is a technical mastery of the knowledge needed to live life well. So it is the craft, skill or expertise of living. But what kind of craft is it really? Certain crafts are done for some external goal, like medicine or archery. They are not done for the sake of themselves, in the sense that the doctor is not doing surgery for the sake of doing surgery, but to promote health. In these crafts the practitioner (surgeon) may do everything perfectly and still miss the target (the patient dies) due to outside events. Inversely the surgeon may make several mistakes and end up with a healthy patient. So while the skill depends on the practitioner the outcome depends on fortune. These are called **stochastic** crafts. Then there are crafts where the goal is contained within the craft itself rather than sought outside of it. So it is achieved wholly via the practitioners skillful performance. An example of these crafts is dancing or perhaps certain games. You can dance only for the sake of dancing. The technical mastery of dancing is enough to achieve the goal, because the goal is to dance skillfully. These crafts are called **performative** or **non-stochastic** crafts. From what I have gathered it seems to be have long been the view among many stoic scholars that virtue is a stochastic craft. The stoic archer is a famous example. I am however currently convinced that it should instead be considered a performative craft. I am mostly influenced and have borrowed some examples here from the scholar Jacob Klein, who argues well for this view \[[here]( and even goes on to claim that virtue as stochastic craft is a misunderstanding and that the "stoic" archer really is a skeptic idea. I have more I would like to say but I wanted to keep this short and hope people will join in discussing it **Do you hold the view that virtue in stoicism is a stochastic craft or that it is a performative craft?**

A relationship won't solve your loneliness. [SEP] I first began browsing this subreddit a couple years ago when I was going through a break-up and needed a way to cope. I read the heartbreaking stories of loneliness from many different walks of life: young and old, men, women and children. My own experience with loneliness is quite simple. My father cheated and divorced my mother shortly after my birth. My father was harsh with my upbringing due to his fears that my mother, who won custody, would raise his son to be a sissy. For most of my schooling, I was able to make a few friends although I battled with social anxiety and low self-esteem. After high school I lost contact with most of my friends. At college I made a few study-buddies but not really true friends. After graduating, I pursued further studies. At that time, I experienced what might have been depression although I was never formally diagnosed. My studies were severely impacted and I barely managed to graduate. Afterwards, I found work at a start-up in a basic administrative position. During that time, I began to think about my life. Despite my desire to do something meaningful in the world, I had wound up being quite average in most regards. I was friendless and worked a job that barely covered my necessities. One day as I was walking home, I was suddenly hit with a deep and profound feeling of loneliness. Two years passed, yet I continued to feel intensely lonely and isolated. At work, I had been promoted a couple times and was no longer doing administrative chores. Despite this, my confidence was quite low. One summer, we temporarily hired a vibrant, energetic university student during her summer break and I was assigned as her supervisor. Over time we grew close and on one occasion she flirted with me but I rejected her advances because of my position as her supervisor . After that incident, I distanced myself from her despite reciprocating her feelings. After she left, my loneliness deepened so I threw myself into my work. Over the next two years, Id successfully coordinated a couple important projects and also managed to make a couple friends through work. I felt fulfilled to an extent. Then one day, out of the blue, an old acquaintance who Id been in contact with over the years began messaging me constantly: from the moment I woke, to when I got ready for bed. Eventually she asked me if I ever had any feelings for her and I candidly admitted that I did at some point. We met for drinks and about a month later, we were in a relationship. It was a rushed decision. While I was a quiet, introverted guy, she was an extravert with a very busy social life that included regular parties and clubbing. I went to a few with her, but I never enjoyed those things and would usually wait in a corner until she was ready to leave. She earned far more than I did and her friends and acquaintances were all in her income bracket. I slowly began to resent that I earned so much less. I hated my old run-down car, especially in comparison to her flashy new car. I hated that I couldnt take her to the sort of fancy restaurants she was accustomed to. I constantly felt like I needed to compensate for lacking so much. Id never felt so inadequate in my life. Several months later, our disparities began to affect the relationship. My insecurities manifested as bitterness and mistrust. My mistrust was an especially huge issue. My fathers betrayal of my mother had made me a very untrusting person and as my girlfriend and I grew apart, I began to become more and more suspicious of her. I never outright accused her of cheating but she could sense my mistrust. We started having frequent arguments and one day she revealed that she was no longer attracted to me and that she had feelings for an ex and wanted to meet him privately to find closure. At this point, perhaps a rational person would have realised that the relationship was over but I had developed an unhealthy attachment and I held on desperately to the fact that she hadnt outright broken up with me. I made all sorts of desperate gestures to win her back like sending her a bouquet at her office and asking her out on dates (all of which she declined). Eventually she grew tired of everything and broke up with me in person. In the ensuing grief, I took some time off from work. I couldnt cope and my performance took a hit. About 5 months later, she messaged to tell me that she had moved on and found someone new. I wished her all the best. As time passed, I was able to look at the things more objectively. Truth was that I felt very lonely in the relationship. She spent most of her time partying and travelling. When we did spend together, she was more engrossed with her phone. We lacked true connection and in the end I felt more like an accessory to her perfect life than an actual partner and companion. I started working on my problems. I began therapy and journaling. Through meditation and introspection, I learned some simple truths. At the end of the day, you have only yourself. Life is rarely filled with constants. People will inevitably come and go as they are swept up in the currents of their own lives; their own goals and desires. You must learn to become comfortable in your solitude. You must take care of your own emotional wellbeing. Its unfair to expect someone to come into your life and magic away all of your suffering. A romantic partner isnt your personal therapist/motivational coach and isnt responsible for your happiness. Getting a partner isnt going to make your depression, anxiety or loneliness disappear. Unhealthy relationships begin when you enter with the mindset that the relationship is going to solve a problem or deficiency in your life. Sadly, many people think, If only I had a girlfriend/boyfriend I would be better off. The truth is that you wont. Thats like bringing a friend into your house that you havent cleaned in years and handing them a broom and telling them, Clean this up. Confront your life! Identify the sources of your pain and deal with them. Clean your own house! It wont be easy, and it may take years (Im certainly far from completing the necessary work), but it will be worth it in the end.

Its true that with a drug or sex or success high you become elevated, but that elevation lacks the sense of whats both below and above. With solitude you stand atop a mighty tower and can see precisely what you have risen above, and more importantly you can see there is nothing above you. Loneliness is personified by cracks in that mighty towers foundation. My neurologist did more than years of regular appointments did- in the span of a little over an hour [SEP] 24, dealt with chronic pain and exhaustion my entire life. I had some sort of episode a while back that landed me in the ER with dilated pupils, red face, a killer headache (I get maybe one headache a year) and a burning feeling in my throat, along with memory loss and trouble speaking. They gave me ibuprofen and discharged me immediately. The memory issues lasted for months, same with the words. Still I struggle with less grip strength in one hand, and a new lazy eye when I get tired (opposite side of my pre-existing one ofc =D) It's been half a year, and I saw the neurologist. She comes in, she's a bit older, we get to talking, I show her a photo of my face the day of the incident. She takes a very long and careful look at it, explains it looks like a sympathetic nervous response. She did a lot of tests in-office, from my balance, to memory, to coordination, to reflexes. So I talk about my chronic pain. She tests my nerves, ranging from my ability to feel vibrations, to scraping at my hands and feet, to poking each finger- ensures there's no damage, asks me many questions about it. Nothing can really be done neurologically, so she recommends I make the rheumatologist appointment and they should help with that. I explain repeated head trauma as a child. We both discuss that the preliminary head MRI showed no damage, she did confirms she did double check that pre-appointment without me even asking. I end up explaining that I get sick easily, am completely out of commission 2ish weeks every time, spent my entire senior year sick. She asks if anyone has ever done immune tests on me- a girl in and out of clinics constantly growing up for being sick with sinus infections- and my answer is no. So she immediately goes "alright, let's do that then" I explain the chronic exhaustion. She asks more questions, specific ones. I elaborate when asked. She asks me if I want to get a sleep study done. She tells me that being unable to do the things I want to do/have to do probably impacts the way I view myself and my capabilities (it absolutely destroys my self esteem). I say yes. She explains one of my vitamins is borderline low, wanted to run a couple more tests for that and start me on the vitamin. I agree. She explains my signs of a potential reoccurring episode are slim, but she wants to do an EEG to be safe. Explains some of the tests, if something is wrong, could be impacting my mental health on a larger scale (I'm diagnosed with BPD and was recently inpatient) but they may take a while to get back. This woman did more for me, listened to me, cared for me, more than **years** of lifetime visits did. I felt heard. For the first time in my life. Holy shit. I wish there were more of her. Egocentrism is the cause of evil [SEP] From personal experience, I have suffered pain, just like everyone else, from people around me, from those we love or feel affection for (not as a complaint or playing the role of victim). In the same way, perhaps I too have hurt others because of my level of egocentrism and lack of empathy. I have tried to understand what it is that drives us or motivates us to act this way toward others. Schopenhauer gave me an important point about the ethics of people: how it helps us to feel compassion and empathy. All of us, as human beings, think for ourselves. Have we ever asked ourselves if we feel empathy for others? Each living being is trapped in their individuality. We do not recognize that the will is one and whole, but it seems to be divided. Yet this is not the cause of pain in the world, nor of the world itself. Living beings are the cause of our own pain and suffering; the origin of pain lies in the ultimate instance of everything: the will. Egoism is the immediate expression of the will in living beings and humans, the direct cause of evil according to Schopenhauer. When egoism arises from the urge to perpetuate itself and to persist in being unique and individual among the totality of other beings, the conflicts of the world erupt. It is because of egoism that most people remain blind to the truth of nature, the essential identity of what is real. _x001C_The monster of the will devours its creatures,_x001D_ according to Schopenhauer. The will alone is eternal and free. Being aware of our nature and of the egoism that separates us from others constitutes the greatest virtue of ethics. To understand the world and its essence as will, and that we are made of the same substance as our fellow beings, has as a consequence that we are capable of putting ourselves in their place and refraining from causing them pain. This is the most virtuous way to act in relation to others. According to Schopenhauer, this is the most coherent and logical way for a human being who is conscious of his own essence and that of the world to act. Experience and example will encourage us to act ethically. Knowing that today it is you and tomorrow it is me is to have the certainty that suffering is universal. This drives us all to act and awakens compassion. From compassion we enter into our most intimate essence: if we find ourselves in the same place as other beings, why increase their suffering by treating them with cruelty instead of compassion? - _x001C_The recognition of the irrational as the dominant force of the universe_x001D_ (Schopenhauer, n.d.).

I'm addicted to escapism [SEP] Weird way to phrase it, but I don't really know how else to say it. I just don't really got much going on in my life. I've struggled with severe mental illness all my life, predominantely depression and anxiety that I've only learned recently are largely linked to my previously undiagnosed BPD. I've always kind of hid from things through videogames and reading as a kid, but now I feel like I don't even have the energy for either of those things. I work a shitty office admin job at a small company that is relatively east and requires maybe two hours of work from me a day, the rest of it I just kind of spend going through reddit, reading, or drawing. Also been SUPER into geoguessr. Fuckin grade A time imo. But, I feel like all I ever do these days is wake up to daydream. Everything I do is to escape from how menial my life is. I wake up, I go to work, I sit in a cubicle for 9 hours alone with my own thoughts and no friends to talk to, I go home, I workout and paint some, I play videogames for 3 hours, I go to bed, I repeat. I like to go out on night walks before bed sometimes, just around the block or so for half an hour or something to get out of the house and almost all the time during the downtime; walks, work, etc, I feel like I just. Am running away from life.I day dream a lot about running away literally - selling everything I own and backpacking across the world just kind of going where the wind takes me. I've had this idea of basically 'how long could I get by being homeless in <foreign country of the day> before I've overstayed my welcome'. 'how far could I stretch <X Money> in <Y Country> before I'd have to stop playing in this fantasy of being able to drop all responsibilities'. Part of why I like GeoGuessr so much is because I can just kind of. Walk around other places. See places I know I'll never get to see. It makes me really sad sometimes, because I'll think about the life I could have had if I grew up somewhere else. Who would I have been? Who would I know? Who would I talk to, and what would I be doing with my life? Would I feel the same that I do now? Sometimes I'll cry about this, because it breaks me how much of life I'm missing out on it feels like - stuck in the middle of nowhere with no prospects of life. I know this is the majority of people and there's things I have to be thankful for, there will always be someone else who has it harder or worse off, but that doesn't make it feel any better. Idk, it's just hard going through the motions every day when all I can think about is the lived experiences of if I was someone else. I'll never get to know what someone elses life is like and that breaks me and I don't know why. I just feel lost, like there's so much that I should be doing and experiencing but can't and never will because of my place in life. I realized the other day that I spend most of my time daydreaming. At work, it's daydreaming about someone else - who I could have been, things I could maybe try to do to spice my life up and make it more interesting, but when I research things they're obviously never as interesting as the fantasy. A lot of my free time at home is spent doing the same - when I'm working out or painting, it's 'what if I grew up in spain? Or Iran? What if I was born on some island, what would my life be like there?'. It's 'what would have happened to me now if I made some extremely drastic choice years ago and followed that impulse?'. When I'm playing games, I'm immersed in the moment, in that character, in who and what they are, that setting - to an almost fanatical level. I participated in fandom culture a lot, but I've never considered myself to be someone on the 'delusional tumblr superwholock' style side of things, I tend to interact with fandom media in a healthy way, but I know that it's more than that for me personally. There's connections and worlds and characters out there that just fascinate me and I realized that it's to the point of escapism because it's not who I am here and now. Sometimes fictional romances feel more impactful to me than real life ones, because it just feels like no one understands the feelings I'm feeling and that any reciprocation is just... pitying me, to a degree. Even on my walks, I'm listening to music and let my mind wander. I'll 'wake up' and be a few blocks away, not even realizing how I got there. I just kept walking forward. Idk. I'm not entirely sure what point I'm trying to make or what kind of discussion I'm trying to spawn off of this, I just wanted to put these thoughts and words out there into the universe and see what happens with it. See what other people think, because I just feel so soulcrushingly alone all the time when it comes to feeling these things, I've never really talked about the extent which I feel like it impacts me before, and I guess I'm just testing the waters on how bad I really need help or if everyone kind of feels this way but just keeps it underwraps too
